RAG_prompt.description: The LLM tier will receive retrieval augmented generation prompt typed as a JSON text, the RAG prompt contain the following field: exploit_type, exploit_content, point_of_interest(optionnal, one or multiples values), sample(optionnal, one or multiples values). Field content and usage is described in this document

request_type.description: The type of request send by the application tier to direct the thinking process of the llm tier

possible_value.name: ioc_guess
possible_value.description: For request of this type the expected comportment is to read data of the next fields to organize a thinking to guess in the end IoC leave by the exploit contained in the request, using sample of noraml behaviour to guess what exploit would leave in those said log

exploit_type.description: Give information about the type of exploit, use this field to understand from where the exploit code is used and what is it targeting

possible_value.name: dos
possible_value.description: Denial-of-service proof-of-concepts or exploits designed to crash, hang, or exhaust resources on a target service or system

possible_value.name: hardware
possible_value.description: Exploits targeting physical hardware, embedded devices, firmware, or dedicated network appliances

possible_value.name: webapps
possible_value.description: Exploits targeting web applications, CMS platforms, APIs, or web interfaces (such as SQL injection, path traversal, CSRF, or web RCE)
possible_value.note: In webapps exploit type, you won't find log from the local execution of the exploit, only log of the taregeted system

possible_value.name: local
possible_value.description: : Exploits requiring access to the target machine first, commonly used for local privilege escalation, unquoted service paths, or local file/process flaws

possible_value.name: remote
possible_value.description: Exploits targeting services or applications over a network without requiring prior local access (such as network daemons, services, or remote code execution flaws).
possible_value.note: In remote exploit type, you won't find log from the local execution of the exploit, only log of the taregeted system

exploit_content.description: This field can be large, it contain the code of the exploit. It's expected for the LLM to understand what actions will perform the exploit, and what traces/IoC it would leave on the system in its log

point_of_interest.description: Point of interest give a brief list of the kind of data you can find in the samples field
point_of_interest.usage: LLM can use point of interest to guide its reflexion on the potential IoC of the inputed exploit

sample.description: Samples are log made by the platform concerned by the inputed exploit. It could be in various format like RFC5424, WinEvents log or custom JSON format
sample.usage: Samples are log displaying a normal behaviour, sample are NOT displaying the use of the exploit
